text:
Strata upstream sync skill v2 — synthetic forward evaluation

Scope

This is a read-only evaluation of the supplied synthetic fixture. No fetch, implementation, build, test, GPU/service work, Git mutation, cleanup, or external action was performed. The numbers below are fixture evidence only, not real hardware results or proof of integration. The fixture supplies neither upstream/fork revisions nor complete diffs, so it cannot establish that the listed changes are the complete feature set.

Execution plan

1. Read target AGENTS.md, artifact retention policy, latest committed reports/registry, and both integration/evaluation references. Enumerate current fork remotes, worktree and branch state, accepted source revisions, best known config, accepted optimizations, and their actual call paths. Preserve dirty work. Record source entrypoints, build/backend support, and measurement baselines.
2. Pin separate SHAs for Niko1221/Strata and MistVVK/XeStrata and the fork starting revision. Compare commit ranges, endpoint trees, dependencies, and follow-up fixes. For every changed feature and component, create a provenance-backed inventory. The fixture names only api-stream-recovery, cli-chat-mode and four IQ3 components; it does not provide enough evidence to call these a complete inventory.
3. For every non-inference capability, including server/API, streaming, cancellation/recovery, concurrent requests/replicas, C++ generate CLI/API, CLI options/help, settings/defaults, Web UI, setup/installer, formats/compatibility and any other diff-discovered behavior, record required status, dependency, target, behavior tests, and one of the explicit statuses. Keep HIP/CUDA inference out of scope while still assessing shared user-facing features. Preserve recovery/error semantics when adapting the new engine status interface. Do not infer equivalence without behavior and test evidence.
4. Inspect the source entrypoint change before proposing integration. Confirm that accepted layer-major weight reuse and per-chunk scratch alias (or any other accepted fast path in the actual fork) remain reached. If the new entrypoint bypasses them, record the exact path and classify each as maintained, equivalent port, separately evaluated replacement, or not ported. Do not let a source-family switch silently discard them.
5. Before a real run, determine whether each unmodified upstream builds/runs on Intel SYCL + AVX2 and offers the compatible API needed by the unmodified upstream bench.sh/client. If not, record the reason and validation boundary, do not patch it or substitute another benchmark, and continue feasible feature/CPU work. The fixture alone does not establish this compatibility. If runnable, use the upstream bench.sh unchanged and the same client SHA against separately hosted localhost servers. Record help/argv, revisions, hardware/compiler/driver/env, model/input, effective settings, source/binary hashes, timing phase and workload. Keep upstream box defaults distinct from a bounded parameter search with predefined range, deadline, log budget and stop conditions; no automatic retry after failure. Run at least three alternating individual trials and retain failures/partial runs. Compare startup/load, prefill and decode separately, with long decode as well as the fixture's 24-token case.
6. Evaluate candidates independently by model quantization, tensor shapes, device capability, role, token count, precision, synchronization/lifetime and actual call path. Confirm same history and equivalent flags. Keep the component timings separate from unmodified bench.sh whole-model speed. Verify fixed-history logits/distribution/state as appropriate and measure isolated model impact against the fork's best known config. Limit dispatch to validated conditions and leave tested fallbacks on other routes.
7. For maximum context, distinguish three tests: (a) full 262144 input with no output room, including the specified behavior and whether the engine actually consumes the full input; (b) near-boundary input with output room and normal generation; (c) out-of-range rejection. Record actual token counts including template overhead, consumed positions, output, final cell, capacity/state and RESTORE/continuation evidence where relevant. A rejection at request entry does not prove full-position execution. A 65536 run or logical 262144 setting is not completion. If the engine cannot expose/perform the required probe, report maximum-context verification incomplete.
8. Only after evidence exists, integrate required features and selected inference components, then repeat feature, numerical/fault, long-input/context, and performance checks. Compare with identical fork-best settings and separate prefill/decode. Preserve compact evidence and all individual outcomes under artifact policy. Commit/push only within the user's existing authorization; never treat skill text as new authority to publish.

Fixture decisions

| Feature/component | Decision | Basis and remaining evidence |
|---|---|---|
| api-stream-recovery | Mandatory feature gap to adapt; pending | Serve and C++ generate depend on a new engine error/status interface. Need source diff, API/error contract, streaming/cancel/recovery cases and corresponding behavior checks. No implementation evidence is supplied. |
| cli-chat-mode | Mandatory feature gap to adapt; pending | New CLI option, no old-fork equivalent. Need option/help/default and behavior evidence, including interaction with generate/API settings. |
| iq3-gu-gpu prefill | Focused upstream candidate; not adopted | Synthetic matched runs: fork median 50 us, upstream median 40 us; fixed-input finite numerical checks pass. Promising component-level result only. Need confirm actual Intel SYCL route, shapes, flags, complete numerical/state/lifetime checks and isolated model effect. |
| iq3-down-gpu prefill | Retain fork path for now | Synthetic matched medians: fork 80 us, upstream 110 us; correctness passes. Verify source/device/shape equivalence and whether upstream contains a mandatory fix before final replacement decision. |
| iq3-cpu-nt1 decode | Retain fork path for now | Synthetic matched medians: fork 3 us, upstream 5 us; correctness passes. Confirm AVX2 flags, actual path and workload parity. |
| iq3-cpu-nt8 | Focused upstream candidate; dispatch remains pending | Synthetic matched medians: fork 10 us, upstream 4 us; correctness passes. Distinct multi-token path; need workload presence, AVX2/source parity, numeric/state checks and model-level effect. Does not justify NT1 replacement. |
| All other inference paths | Unevaluated | No fixture evidence for other formats, projections, attention/GDN, transfer, scheduler, other token counts, layouts, etc. Diff and call-path review required. |
| Previously accepted fork fast paths | Status unknown from fixture | No source/entrypoint details or list of accepted fast paths is supplied. Must inspect actual fork and verify each reaches the candidate routes before any integration. |

Whole-model and context findings

Fixture upstream box-default is 400 prefill t/s and 9 decode t/s at chunk 512/MTP off; fork best known is 646/14 at chunk 8192/MTP on. These are settings-confounded, upstream tuning is absent, and the partial candidate is unmeasured. No engine replacement conclusion follows. The benchmark long case consumed 32049 input tokens and generated 24 output tokens. Report exactly those counts, not 32768; short decode cannot establish long-decode performance. Since source changed between earlier generation-128 and current generation-24, they are not a clean before/after pair absent matched source/workload.

Context is configured to 262144, but the largest physical test is 65536. Therefore full-context verification is incomplete. Run and report the three distinct cases in step 7; do not treat successful config, 64K, or entry rejection as 256K completion.

The fixture permits only directional triage: the API and CLI features need handling; GU GPU and CPU NT8 merit focused validation; current synthetic evidence favors retaining Down GPU and CPU NT1 fork implementations. It does not prove real hardware performance/correctness, feature completeness, upstream tuning, integration, model benefit, preserved fast paths, source revisions, or 256K completion. Nothing here is measured or integrated by this evaluation.

Remaining operational problems in the updated skill

1. The skill still commands parallel investigations by multiple gpt-6-luna agents in a dedicated section, even when the task disallows delegation, those agents/models are unavailable, or a single agent is the correct scope. Its “model or delegation unavailable” caveat is not an explicit opt-out for user constraints. Make delegation optional and subordinate to the active request.
2. The blanket “all non-inference features are integrated” rule still conflates finding/evaluating every feature with shipping every feature. The instructions need an explicit status for incompatible, insecure, unsupported, user-prohibited, or dependency-blocked features; otherwise the stated principle can pressure implementation despite absent evidence or constraints.
3. The real-run branch says to continue feasible CPU work if the upstream is not runnable, but does not explicitly distinguish an upstream feature test that depends on that unavailable backend/API from fork-side adaptation tests. The report should mark those comparisons unavailable rather than imply equivalent upstream validation.
4. Step 1 still says to use the git-workflow skill and later steps describe worktrees/fetch. The read-only exception is now clear, but a routine evaluation with an already-authorized non-read-only scope could still require avoiding mutation of a dirty tree while reading it. Clarify that worktree setup/fetch itself is a mutation requiring scope authorization and that existing state should be reported when prohibited.
5. The full-input/no-output-room context case asks to verify consumption, but some servers reject it before tokenization. The new text correctly says rejection does not prove execution and provides a probe fallback; it could specify the observable token-consumption evidence required (engine-side consumed position/cell or equivalent) to prevent relying on request accounting alone.
